uncited: **Inputs:** An optimized set of 3D Gaussians $\mathcal{G} = \{G_i\}_{i=1}^M$, where each $G_i$ has position $\mathbf{p}_i$, covariance $\mathbf{\Sigma}_i$, opacity $\alpha_i$, and color attributes.
A set of training views with known camera poses and intrinsics.
**Rendered Depth Map:** A 2D array $D \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times W}$ storing the median depth of splats projected to each pixel.
**Rendered Normal Map:** A 2D array $N \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times W \times 3}$ storing the surface normal in camera space for each pixel.

**Oriented Point Cloud:** A list of points $P = \{(\mathbf{x}_j, \mathbf{n}_j, \mathbf{c}_j)\}_{j=1}^K$, where $\mathbf{x}_j$ is the 3D position, $\mathbf{n}_j$ is the normal, and $\mathbf{c}_j$ is the color.
**Render Depth:** For each training view, project all 3D Gaussians to 2D.
**Derive Normals:** Convert the rendered depth map $D$ back into 3D space to derive the corresponding normal map $N$.
*   Retrieve the depth $d = D[u, v]$ and normal $\mathbf{n}_{cam} = N[u, v]$.
*   Unproject the pixel coordinates and depth to obtain the 3D position $\mathbf{x}$ in world space.
*   Transform the normal $\mathbf{n}_{cam}$ to world space.
*   Retrieve the color $\mathbf{c}$ from the RGB image at $(u, v)$.
*   **Depth Level:** The depth of the octree used in Poisson reconstruction.
*   **Point Count:** The number of points in the input cloud.
*   **Time Complexity:** Dominated by the rendering of depth/normal maps for all training views and the octree construction in Poisson reconstruction.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Proportional to the number of training views and the resolution of the depth/normal maps, plus the memory for the 2 million point cloud and octree.
